title: Seven-day weather gave no clear repeated change in insect catch temperature slopes in Sweden and Madagascar in 2019-2020
abstract: We tested whether a fixed seven-day weather window changed temperature slopes compared with the actual insect collection interval. Four models used 5,805 measured catches in Sweden and Madagascar in 2019-2020. All four corrected intervals for the paired slope change included zero. Mean absolute temperature differences were 0.15-0.18 C in Sweden and 0.01 C in Madagascar. Most collection intervals were seven integer days. A shorter time-block model gave a clear change in later Sweden. The results do not establish that windows are equivalent. One survey year per country, selected catches, coarse weather and few time clusters limit inference. We provide code, source hashes, aggregate results and direct window checks.

display.caption: Paired temperature slope changes and mean absolute weather mismatch in four country-period samples. Dark intervals have 95 percent nominal coverage; pale intervals correct for four tests.

citations.reason: Duration scaling study motivates a distinct audit of weather-window definitions; source catch records overlap.
We adapt the MIT catch/weather loader and retrieval code. Our target is the paired slope change when the exposure window changes.
